description: Swiss labour cost simulation module with canton-level fiscal profiles. Version 1 combines national social contributions, standard occupational pension assumptions, accident insurance assumptions and canton-level withholding-tax placeholders.

ahv_iv_eo.source_note: Official Swiss federal social contribution rate, split equally between employee and employer.

unemployment_insurance.source_note: Standard unemployment insurance contribution rate up to the insured salary ceiling.

occupational_pension_lpp.source_note: The LPP/BVG component is standardized. Actual pension contributions vary by age, pension plan and employer scheme.

accident_insurance.source_note: Accident insurance rates vary by insurer, firm risk class and sector. The module uses standardized benchmark rates for comparability.

withholding_tax.source_note: Canton-level withholding-tax tables are published by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration. They will be integrated in a second step.

ordinary_tax.note: Ordinary assessment (taxation ordinaire / imposition ordinaire / ordentliche Veranlagung), the annual tax-return regime applying to Swiss citizens and C-permit holders, as opposed to withholding tax at source (foreign workers without a C permit). Combines federal (impot federal direct, single national scale), cantonal (each canton's own base scale and mechanism) and communal (the reference municipality's own multiplier) income tax. Full computation engine: analysis/switzerland/swiss_ordinary_tax_2026.py -- that file's docstring documents the exact mechanism used for each canton (marginal brackets, flat rate, marginal-with-cliff, whole-income interpolated rate, or Basel-Landschaft's continuous logarithmic formula) and Geneva's bespoke multi-stage centimes-additionnels calculation. See switzerland_sources_2026.json for exact source URLs and legal article citations per canton.

cantonal_and_communal_multipliers_2026.source: ESTV/SSK, "Taux et coefficients d'impots" / "Steuersatz und Steuerfuss", section 3.4.1, etat de la legislation au 1er janvier 2026 -- cantonal capitals only
cantonal_and_communal_multipliers_2026.note: Where a canton's own Kantonsblatt cited a different numeric multiplier than this consolidated table (found for OW and ZG), the canton-specific Kantonsblatt figure was used instead, as a more directly-cited primary source -- see switzerland_sources_2026.json.

BS.note: no separate communal tax at the cantonal capital

VS.note: no cantonal-level multiplier by law; the barreme gives the cantonal tax directly

GE.note: bespoke multi-stage mechanism, see engine docstring

methodological_limits: The module is not an individual Swiss payslip calculator.
Occupational pension contributions are standardized and do not reproduce firm-level pension plans.
Accident insurance rates are benchmark assumptions and do not reflect sector-specific risk classes.
The selected canton is represented by a reference municipality for comparability (the cantonal capital in every case).

Ordinary assessment: family quotient / income-splitting mechanisms (relevant for married or single-parent households, e.g. Vaud's quotient familial) are not modeled, consistent with this module's single/childless reference profile.

Ordinary assessment: aggregate income+wealth tax caps ('bouclier fiscal' / 'Hoechstbelastung' / 'freno all'imposta', in effect in Bern, Lucerne, Basel-Stadt, Aargau, Vaud, Valais, Ticino, Geneva and others) are not modeled, since this module does not compute wealth tax.
Ordinary assessment: church tax is not modeled, consistent with the withholding-tax module's existing convention.

Ordinary assessment: capital pension payments and liquidation gains, taxed separately at reduced rates by nearly every canton, are not modeled (irrelevant for this module's standard-employment reference profile).

Ordinary assessment, Basel-Landschaft (BL): the continuous logarithmic formula uses the base (2005) legislative parameters; the annual cold-progression re-indexation to the current tax year is not reproduced -- medium confidence.

Ordinary assessment, Fribourg (FR) and Valais (VS): both cantons' own law states that a single average tax rate applies to the whole income and interpolates continuously within each income class; this module approximates that continuous interpolation using the discrete class boundaries actually sourced, rather than the full official schedule (published at CHF 100 increments).
